title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 112-114, 'Ateliers', July 1986). Grothendieck is axiomatizing a 'spatios' Σ. This is an ordered set of 'figures' (non-empty compact parts) with Sup, Inf and a complement operation ∁. Σ is apparently not itself a Boolean algebra, for example a lattice of closed or compact sets with ∁ = closure of the set-complement.

Setup from p.112. A discrete figure 𝔄 is a finite family of non-empty, mutually disjoint elements of Σ; these form Figspatdisc(Σ). Refinement is defined by 𝔅 ≪ 𝔄 iff every b ∈ 𝔅 lies below some a ∈ 𝔄. For a ∈ 𝔄, put 𝔅_a = {b ∈ 𝔅 : b ≤ a}, a' = Sup 𝔅_a ≤ a, and a'' = a ∧ ∁a', the 'remainder' of a not covered by the finer pieces.

Lemma 2 (this page). For B ≪ A, the following are equivalent.
(i) A ∪ B lies in some Σ' ⊂ Σ that is stable under Sup, Inf and ∁ and is a Boolean algebra for the induced order and complement.
(ii) Two conditions hold:
  (a) every a ∈ A satisfies a = a' ∨ a'', i.e. a = (Sup 𝔅_a) ∨ (a ∧ ∁ Sup 𝔅_a);
  (b) B̂ = B ∪ {a'' : a'' ≠ 0} is 'admissible' (defined around p.110). This presumably means a disjoint family whose finite joins form a Boolean subalgebra Σ_B̂ = 𝔅(B̂) of Σ.
Addendum: under these conditions, Σ_B̂ is the smallest Σ' satisfying (i). One then calls the pair {A, B} admissible.

The page then begins an axiom 'At-0-VV²'. For F ≪ G in the distinguished family 𝔉, form A and B from the interiors X⁰ of the members. The axiom (p.114) asserts that {A, B} is admissible. The next page announces the generalization from pairs to flags F_0 ≪ … ≪ F_n, read as flags of discrete figures A_0 ≪ … ≪ A_n. These must be simultaneously embeddable in one Boolean subalgebra.

Purpose: guarantee that successive refinements of a 'figure' (partition-like data) behave like a common finite Boolean subdivision. This is an axiom of combinatorial/tame-geometric flavour on the poset of figures.

Check of the lemma.
- (i)⇒(ii): in a Boolean Σ', a = a' ∨ (a ∧ ¬a') always holds. B̂ is pairwise disjoint (a'' ≤ ∁b for b ≤ a, and distinct a's are disjoint), and its joins lie in Σ'.
- (ii)⇒(i): take Σ' = 𝔅(B̂). It contains B, and by (a) each a is the join of members of B̂.
- Minimality: any Σ' as in (i) contains a'' = a ∧ ∁a', hence contains B̂.
The argument is sound, modulo the exact definition of 'admissible', which is not on this page.
errors: Previous page (p.112) writes a'' = b ∧ ∁b'; this must be a'' = a ∧ ∁a', as used on this page.

In the axiom, F ≪ G is followed by B := interiors of G and A := interiors of F. This seems inverted relative to the lemma's convention B ≪ A (B finer), unless ≪ is read with the opposite orientation; a notational slip is likely.
The lemma's statement depends on the definition of 'admissible' (cf. p.110), which is not reproduced. The equivalence is only as precise as that definition.
The next page itself says 'Ceci n'est pas vrai[?]', indicating Grothendieck found the pairwise axiom insufficient and moved to flags.

ideas.what: A finite family of elements of a lattice with complement lies in a Boolean subalgebra iff a 'commutation' decomposition a = (a ∧ c) ∨ (a ∧ ∁c) holds and the resulting atoms form an admissible disjoint family.
ideas.modern_name: Compatibility/commutativity of elements in ortho(-modular) lattices; Boolean blocks; Foulis–Holland-type criteria
ideas.usually_credited_to: Birkhoff–von Neumann (1936), Foulis, Holland (1960s), Kalmbach (Orthomodular Lattices, 1983)

ideas.what: Axiom requiring that refinements F ≪ G of distinguished figures (via interiors) be admissible pairs, to be generalized to flags F_0 ≪ … ≪ F_n.
ideas.modern_name: Common refinement / simultaneous Boolean subdivision axiom in an axiomatic tame/combinatorial geometry
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; loosely related to o-minimal cell decomposition (van den Dries) and to point-free (locale/mereotopology) approaches
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions tame topology only in general terms; this axiomatics is unpublished

missed.claim: Condition (ii)(a) is exactly the commutativity condition of orthomodular-lattice theory (a C c iff a = (a∧c) ∨ (a∧c⊥)). The lemma is a version of 'pairwise compatible finite sets generate a Boolean block'. Grothendieck re-derives quantum-logic compatibility inside his axiomatics of geometric figures, a link not made in the literature on his tame-topology program.
missed.quote: a) ∀a ∈ A, on a a = a' ∨ a'' ... l'alg. de Boole Σ_B̂ engendrée par B̂ ... le plus petit des sous-ens. Σ' satisfaisant (i)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This could situate his 'spatios' within known lattice theory (ortholattices, mereotopology), clarifying which of his axioms are standard and which are new.

missed.claim: Axiom At-0-VV² for refinements, and its announced extension to flags of discrete figures, is left in draft form. The next page doubts its sufficiency.
missed.quote: Axiome At-0-VV² ... toute F ≪ G avec F, G ∈ 𝔉, posons B = {X⁰ | X ∈ G}, A = {X⁰ | X ∈ F}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is minor. It is part of an unpublished point-free axiomatization of tame geometry that could be compared with o-minimal/semialgebraic stratification axioms.

deep.surprise_reason: The lemma is a routine lattice-theoretic statement, essentially standard compatibility in ortholattices. The interest is only in its role within an unpublished 1986 axiomatization of 'spatios'/figures.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: 'a'' = b ∧ ∁b'' should read a'' = a ∧ ∁a'.
'On[?] toute F ≪ G' is likely 'Pour toute F ≪ G'; 'F, G ∈ 𝔉[?]' refers to the family 𝔉 ⊂ 𝔓(𝒜) of p.112.
Next page 'Soit Σ un spectre[?]' very likely reads 'Soit Σ un spatios'.
Next page 'Fig opt' should read 'Figspat' (Fig spat disc).
